text: Joeri Verlinden, born on 22 January 1988, is a Dutch swimmer specializing in butterfly and freestyle. He is currently trained by Martin Truijens and was previously trained by Marcel Wouda. He made his international debut at the European Short Course Swimming Championships 2006 in Helsinki, where he competed in all butterfly events, finishing 34th in the 50 m, 32nd in the 100 m, and 27th in the 200 m butterfly. At the 2007 Dutch Open Swim Cup, he qualified for the European LC Championships in his hometown of Eindhoven. At the European Championships in March 2008, he placed 16th in the 50 m butterfly and 11th in the 100 m butterfly, missing the 2008 Summer Olympics by 0.23 seconds; he finished 21st in the 200 m butterfly. In April 2008, he competed at the FINA Short Course World Championships, finishing ex-aequo 17th in the 50 m butterfly and 16th in the 100 m. As part of the 4 × 100 m medley relay, he swam a national record alongside Bastiaan Tamminga, Robin van Aggele, and Mitja Zastrow, securing 8th place in the final. Verlinden qualified for the 2016 Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro in the 100 meter butterfly.
